question.text: The vertices of a hyperbola <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> and its eccentricity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msqrt><mn>5</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math>. Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> be the normal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> at a point in the first quadrant and parallel to the line <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>. If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>d</mi></math> is the length of the line segment of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math> between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></math> and the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>-axis then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is equal to _____ .

solution.text:
Given equation of hyperbola is

H:x236-y29=1

Any point on the hyperbola is P6secθ,3tanθ.

Equation of normal is

6xcosθ+3ycotθ=45

Also, this normal is parallel to the line 2x+y=22, therefore slope of both lines must be equal , hence

-2sinθ=-2

⇒sinθ=12

⇒θ=π4

Equation of normal is

2x+y=15

And, this normal intersects y-axis at K, so

P≡62,3 and K≡0,15.

So,

PK2=d2=62-02+3-152

⇒d2=216
